ShortDescription.Value: Build a ski resort: drawn chairlifts, gondolas and an aerial tram, runs on the game's own snow, lodges and a resort economy. Base game only.

Publish.LongDescription:
**Build a ski resort in Cities: Skylines II.**
Draw chairlifts, gondolas and an aerial tram up your mountain, draw runs down it, and let the game's own snow decide when they open. Guests ski, buy tickets and lessons, and the resort draws tourists to your city. Base game only: no other mod is required.
## Highlights - **Four lifts, one tool.** Fixed-grip triple chairlift, detachable quad chairlift, gondola and aerial tram. Click the base station, click the top, and the tool plans numbered towers over your terrain. Chairs and cabins ride the cable. - **Runs on real snow.** Draw natural, groomed, snowmaking, night and cat track runs. Each is rated green to double black from its hardest pitch, and opens at 3 feet (91 cm) of snow. Snow guns extend the season where it is cold enough. - **Seasons.** Snow melts in spring, runs close and lifts stop. The aerial tram keeps running as summer sightseeing. - **Lodges, Ski School and Ski Patrol.** Five lodges, a school and two patrol buildings, each following a real place. - **Ski Bus Depot.** A coach stop in town that brings guests to a hill too far away to draw them on its own. - **One panel.** The Ski Resort button (top left) opens Attraction, Runs, Lifts, Guests, Finances and History views, plus a problem list that flies you to what is wrong. - **A resort economy.** Lift tickets, season passes, lessons, lodge spend and running costs. A ski area's attraction score feeds the game's tourism, so a bigger resort brings more visitors.
## Requirements Cities: Skylines II 1.6 (tested on 1.6.2f1). No other mod and no DLC. Start from a new city.
## Getting started 1. Open the Ski Resort panel. Place a Welcome Sign snapped to a road (it stands set back from it). Then place a lodge near where the runs will be. 2. Pick a lift type. Place the base station, then the top station facing it, then draw the line between them. Press Enter to build. 3. Connect a low-voltage power line to the base station. 4. Draw runs downhill from the top station, and wait for snow.
## Good to know - Skiers are counted, not simulated. Chairs and cabins move but carry no riders, and the chairs do not sway in the wind. - Stations sit on the slope as placed, so on steep ground one can end up partly in the hillside. Move It lifts it out (see Works with). - Chairlifts and gondolas stop in summer when no run is open. The aerial tram keeps running as sightseeing. - Bulldozing a Welcome Sign also deletes every run linked to it, with the runs' glade trees, and the run fees are not refunded. A warning shows the run count and asks first. To move a sign, use Relocate in its info panel: its runs stay linked. - The Resort Planner (outline a slope, get proposed lifts and a set of runs) is experimental and off by default: turn it on in Options. It builds the runs only: you build its proposed lifts yourself with the lift tool. On steep ground it plans mostly black runs with few greens. Roads, buildings and lift stations inside the outline are not avoided, and its Undo ends when the tool closes. - Lifts are power-line networks and need low-voltage power at the base station. The game refuses a city high-voltage line at a lift. - Before uninstalling, bulldoze your lifts and runs (or use the Delete all ski resort content button in the mod's Options), then save the city. Otherwise run paint can stay in the saved terrain, and what leftover lift pieces do is untested. - Resorts cost money all year and earn in winter. Build in steps.
## Guides and details Step-by-step guides, every number, settings and troubleshooting are on the docs site: {{DOCS_URL}} Start with the Resort Quickstart at {{DOCS_URL}}/quickstart/ and the Lifts guide at {{DOCS_URL}}/guides/lifts/. Bug reports: the Paradox forum thread {{FORUM_URL}} or the Discord thread {{DISCORD_URL}}. Source code: {{GITHUB_URL}}
## Works with Nothing else is required, but Move It is highly recommended: lift stations sit on the slope as placed, and on steep ground they can end up partly in the hillside. Move It works on every building and station. Write Everywhere is recommended too: with it, the Welcome Sign shows your ski area's name (without it, the name board stays plain). If Tourism Overhaul, Realistic Workplaces and Households or a trip-planner mod is installed, the panel shows a notice and changes nothing in them. Realistic Trips replaces the game's leisure system that ski days need: with it, the resort sends no skiers of its own. Lifts, runs, snow and buildings still work.
## Credits - Modular Golf Course Pack by joergeske: the modular recreation idea this mod grew from. - Meapy's Tourism Overhaul: studied for how tourism and attractions work. Not required. - The fixed-grip lift is a tribute to the Pallavicini lift at Arapahoe Basin. - Built with Claude (Anthropic) for decompilation, prefab work and asset generation; direction and testing by the author. - Full credits and licenses: {{DOCS_URL}}/credits/

- Save compatible with previous: n/a (first release) - Layout versions: Binding 1, TreeMember 2, SeasonPass 1, HistoryMonth 2, MonthInProgress 2, RunPropMember 1, RunPropSettings 1, LodgeNumber 1, TrackSnow 1, RunName 1 - Do not load in older versions: no
First public release.
- Four lift types: fixed-grip triple chairlift, detachable quad chairlift, gondola and aerial tram. Chairs and cabins move along the cable; the tram shuttles two cabins. - One lift tool: click the base station and the top station, click the line to add a tower, drag to move one, Enter builds. The tower planner fits tower heights to the terrain with few towers, prefers short towers next to the stations, and draws spans that are too steep in red. Towers are numbered. - Ski runs you draw: natural, groomed, snowmaking, night and cat track, each rated green to double black from its slope. - Cat track tool: lay out a track, and one key grades the ground under 25 percent and builds the cat track on it. Where it crosses a run it grades up to 2 m inside the run and keeps the run's difficulty. Delete mode (Ctrl+Shift+D) and a hub trash button remove a track; right click and Esc never do. - Resort Planner (experimental): outline a slope of up to 9 km2 and the planner proposes lifts and a set of linked runs around them, grouped in pods, with each lift's way home (green, blue, black only, or ride the lift down). Leave out runs, pods or lifts, set the number of lifts, the way home, the mix and the run kinds, then build the runs in one go and undo them; the proposed lifts you build yourself with the lift tool. The scan runs in the background with a progress line, and right click stops it. Optional tree filler. Ctrl+Shift+Q; it is off by default and is turned on in Options. - Safety Net Fence: decorative orange netting on thin poles, in the hub's Runs tab. - Snow-depth run system: runs open at 3 ft (91 cm) on 60 percent of the run and stay open while 1 ft covers 40 percent, snow guns on snowmaking and night runs (two months before winter to one month after), powder days, seasons. - Snow guns, hydrants and floodlights stand at a set distance along a run's edge, however its outline was drawn, with two values per run in the Runs view. Cat tracks carry guns and hydrants on one side, and pay snowmaking upkeep by plan area while their guns can run; with the gun value at Off, none, and snow already made stays until it melts. - Welcome Sign (set back 8 m from the road on a leveled lot), five lodges, Ski School, two patrol buildings. - Ski Bus Depot: a coach stop in town for the nearest ski area, at any distance. A home closer to it than to a lodge starts its ski day there; guests pay as at a lodge. It adds no capacity and no score, needs a lodge on the hill, and bills 1,500 a month plus 300 per km to that lodge (Finances, row Ski bus). An oxblood coach, with SKI BUS painted on it, drives between the depot and the hill. Selecting the coach or the depot shows a Ski Bus card beside the game's panel: guests by bus this month, the coach bill and the distance to the hill lodge. - The Ski Resort panel: Attraction, Runs, Lifts, Guests, Finances and History views, a problem list and a build strip. - Economy: lift tickets, season passes, lessons, lodge spend, off-season half staff. - Delete all ski resort content, a button in the mod's Options (Reset group): removes everything the mod placed in the loaded city, after a confirmation, to clean a city before uninstalling. It cannot be undone. - Works on the base game; no other mod is required. Move It is highly recommended and Write Everywhere is recommended. - Known limitations: a hill far from the city's homes and hotels gets few ski-day guests (the panel shows the distance), chairs carry no riders, the chairs do not sway in wind, stations can sit partly in the hillside on steep ground, chairlifts and gondolas stop in summer.
